newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee pares gains by close, seen vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee pares gains by close, seen vulnerable.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures were knocked down by local selling towards the close on Wednesday but the market still finished the day higher.
Traders said some arbitrage selling against New York was also seen.
Benchmark September lost some $9-$10 in the eleventh-hour as locals unloaded their long positions. It still finished $55 higher at $1,560 per tonne after a high of $1,575.
The contract had risen by some $60 in the morning in line with market expectations. The gains were more or less sustained in the afternoon by advancing New York arabica futures.
"New York-wise, the market had been pushed down too far. So there's plenty of room to recover," said one trader.
While the U.S. market showed further upside potential, robustas in London could lag behind with September's rise seen capping at $1,600.
On Wednesday, the market tumbled to six-month lows of $1,477 basis the second-month contract, thus keeping origin sellers at bay.
"We see more hedge selling from Uganda or Madagascar at the $1,600 level," the trader said.
The day's volume was 2,969 lots with September and November contracts accounting for 2,500 lots.
Switch buying was the order of the day, with Sept/Nov traded at around $10.
New York arabicas continued its rally on the back of heavy speculative and trade buying on fears of a shortage of exchange-certified coffee for delivery against front-month September.
Sept/Dec switch widened after the failure of a large quantity of coffee posted for grading to be certified.
"From a technical perspective, the New York rally means little on the second month continuous series chart, but there is little preventing a test of resistance at $1.7850," broker GNI said.
It also said a rally today above $1,533 in London would suggest that the break on Tuesday was a bear trap.
In other news, Ivorian cocoa and coffee exporters said the government was likely to raise its reference cocoa and coffee farm gate prices in the 1997/98 (Oct-Sept) season.

Donors in 1996/97 have pushed for increases as part of talks on disbursement of outstanding amounts of a $150 million agricultural sector adjustment loan from the World Bank. Coffee prices were set 200 CFA lower at 495 CFA a kg for 1996/97.
Weather in Brazil's coffee regions is forecast to remain mild for the next five days -- well into the end of the month when the country's frost season typically ends.
